newsitem.title: UK: British MP wins damages from Soviet defector.
newsitem.headline: British MP wins damages from Soviet defector.

text.p: British MP George Robertson received a public apology and undisclosed damages on Wednesday from a Soviet defector who falsely accused him of tabling a parliamentary question for the Soviet secret police.

Oleg Gordievsky and Macmillan, publishers of his autobiography "Next Stop Execution", were also ordered to pay costs after his lawyer admitted in London's High Court that there was no truth to the allegations.
Gordievsky had alleged that Robertson, the opposition Labour Party's spokesman for Scotland, had abused his position as a member of parliament and betrayed Britain in 1987 by acting for the KGB.

"I am pleased that my reputation has been publicly vindicated and that Mr Gordievsky and Macmillan have acknowledged the wholly untrue nature of the serious allegations made about me in the book," Roberston said in a statement.
"The idea that I would table a parliamentary question on the suggestion of the Soviet Union's secret police, the KGB, would have been laughable if it was not so sinister."
Last year, former Labour leader Michael Foot received damages and a public apology after he was described as a Soviet agent in a serialisation of the book in The Sunday Times newspaper.
